headline: Anthropic logged net loss of over $80 billion in first half of 2026
snippet: Anthropic's net loss widened sharply to $80.7 billion in the first half of this year, in large part due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into shares of the AI startup, according to a draft prospectus for a planned initial public offering that was reviewed by Reuters. The San Francisco-based company is expected to go public in November and some investors are now weighing a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion following its latest financial disclosures, Reuters reported last week. Its first-half loss, widening from a loss of $13 billion a year earlier, included a $72 billion accounting charge reflecting an increase in the estimated value of bonds that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash costs tied to its operations, the document said. The disclosures underscore the hefty costs of the AI race even as investors give greater scrutiny to whether the vast sums being poured into chips and data centers will generate sufficient returns. Anthropic has committed to spending at least $518 billion over a decade on cloud services, computing and infrastructure. The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half, up from $2.3 billion a year earlier, the S-1 document showed. Anthropic did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. Financing costs At an investor meeting on October 14, Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. While the figures eased some concerns about the enormous costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate. Revenue had more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6 billion in the second quarter. A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, ahead of rival OpenAI's potential listing next year. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic posted a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, with most of that stemming from a similar accounting charge. As Anthropic's valuation climbed, the estimated fair value of those notes tripled year over year. Excluding the charge, Anthropic posted an operating loss of about $8.1 billion on $4.6 billion of revenue in 2025. The company has benefited from the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps.

headline: UNMIK chief welcomes signs of an end to Kosovo's political deadlock but warns of heightened tensions and urges Belgrade and Pristina to advance dialogue
snippet: The head of the United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) has warned the Security Council of 'increased tensions in Kosovo and the region' over the past six months, whilst welcoming emerging signs that the country's institutional deadlock is easing. Presenting the UN secretary-general's latest report in New York, Peter Due noted that despite peaceful, inclusive parliamentary elections on June 7-the third vote in 16 months-the period was marked by 'political uncertainty and heightened rhetoric.' Due welcomed the election around midnight on 6 October of Justina Shiroka-Pula as President of Kosovo, making her the third woman to assume the role. 'Political disagreement is part of the fabric of democratic life, but prolonged institutional deadlock carries consequences. The formation of the institutions is therefore encouraging,' Due said, observing that the prolonged political impasse 'seems to have been broken.' Insisting that 'accountability remains essential to building trust,' Due urged authorities in Belgrade and Pristina to cooperate fully in prosecuting those responsible for the 2023 Banjska attack and the 2024 strike on the Iber-Lepenc water canal. He stressed that tangible progress requires genuine commitment from both parties in the European Union-facilitated dialogue. 'Our shared responsibility is to work for reconciliation and normalisation, so that all communities in Kosovo can participate fully and confidently in public life, with respect for the rule of law, human rights and Kosovo's multiethnic character,' Due added. Addressing the Council, Kosovo Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca defended the country's record, stating that 'Kosovo continues to remain one of the most stable democracies in southeastern Europe.' Konjufca rejected allegations within the report, criticising 'the misuse of ethnic connotations and fabrications' and accusing critics of misrepresenting standard law-enforcement measures as ethnically motivated violations.

headline: Bulgaria to Attract Private Capital for Infrastructure through Public-Private Partnerships and Concessions, PM Says
snippet: The state will attract private capital to develop infrastructure through public-private partnerships and concessions, Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters on Tuesday. He said the aim is to reserve public funds for healthcare, education and support for small and remote communities. The Prime Minister was speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony for a battery park for electricity storage in Tvarditsa, in the southeastern Sliven Region. Asked about addressing economic disparities between regions and encouraging investment, Radev highlighted the need to improve transport connectivity as a priority. He said poor connectivity is a problem for remote regions and small communities. State budget resources were limited, and this connectivity could not be developed through public funding alone, even over decades, the Prime Minister said. Radev said the government is tightening controls and reviewing every public procurement contract. He added that a change in the underlying philosophy and approach to infrastructure development is under way, with private capital being attracted. Asked whether the government will support businesses in response to rising electricity prices, the Prime Minister said a clear plan has been drawn up. He said the Energy Minister has met businesspeople and further talks are planned to determine how the government can provide assistance in the most appropriate and effective way. Radev said the energy crisis is affecting Europe as a whole and identified the abandonment of efficient energy resources as one of its causes. He added that the crisis is global and reiterated his call for an end to the war. Asked to comment on a protest scheduled for Tuesday evening under the slogan "Your 'peace' is capitulation! Your 'diplomacy' is isolation!", Prime Minister Radev said the organizers' intentions are becoming increasingly clear: "to resurrect the 'assemblage' and to whitewash GERB leader Boyko Borissov and Movement for Rights and Freedoms (MRF) leader Delyan Peevski, to return to power alongside them because they cannot do so on their own, to drag us into the war, and to have Assen Vassilev draw up our budget, which will finish us off." The "assemblage" refers to a government formula in June 2023 – April 2024 under which the Continue the Change – Democratic Bulgaria coalition collaborated with its political opponent GERB in a bid to restore political stability. Assen Vassilev was finance minister under the "assemblage" arrangement. GERB's Borissov and MRF's Peevski, and the political model associated with them, have been blamed for the spread of political corruption.
